newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks bounce back after early selloff.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks bounce back after early selloff.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks roared back into the plus column Tuesday after shaking off an early bout of profit taking.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 13.57 points at 7,785.66, having rebounded swiftly from a morning loss of more than 50 points.
But in the broader market, declining issues still led advances 12-10 on active volume of 324 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 7.52 points to 1,439.47 as several technology stocks posted strong gains.

Analysts said the latest batch of economic data, including the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for May, showed that inflation remained in check, further strengthening Wall Street's belief that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates when it meets in early July.
But the data gave investors a chance to take profits and a pause from last week's record-breaking rally, they said.
Dan Ascani, director of research at Global Market Strategists Inc., said he expected the market to gain further ground.
Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management, said the Dow's initial softness was a well-deserved "breather" but that there was little to keep the market restrained for long.
"I think the market is going to do what it is going to do, no matter what the economic statistics are," he said.
The government said the CPI inched up 0.1 percent last month. Excluding the often-volatile food and energy components, the core CPI rose 0.2 percent, in line with Wall Street's forecasts.
In another report, housing starts for May fell 4.8 percent to a seasonally adjusted rate of 1.397 million compared to a revised rate of 1.468 million in April.
May industrial output rose 0.4 percent vs. economists' forecast for a rise of 0.2 percent.
Intel Corp. surged 1-7/8 to 149-1/8 while Dell Computer Corp. gained 4 to 119-3/8. Dell said it was very pleased with its current quarter and sees no slowing of momentum in Europe.
International Business Machines Corp. gained 7/8 to 90-1/4 and Digital Equipment Co. climbed 1-3/8 to 38.
Equifax Inc., which will be added to the Standard & Poor's 500 stock index after June 18, bounced 3-3/8 to 35-1/2.
Lucent Technologies Inc. gained 2-3/4 to 70-1/2 after it announced a consumer products venture with Philips Electronics NV valued at $2.5 billion.
NCR Corp. said it expected quarterly results to be below estimates due to weak revenues and disappointing hardware systems orders. NCR fell 1-3/8 to 28-7/8.
Amgen Inc. fell sharply after the company said it expected its sales growth to slow for its Epogen drug. Amgen lost 2-3/8 to 59-3/4.
